source_date: 2023-11 (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AFib Guideline) + 2020 AGA IDA Guideline

entries.title: Anticoagulate AFib patients with annual stroke risk ≥2%/yr (≈ CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2 men, ≥3 women)
entries.snippet: In patients with AF and an estimated annual thromboembolic risk of ≥2% per year, oral anticoagulation is recommended. CHA2DS2-VASc remains the most widely studied risk score; a score of ≥2 in men or ≥3 in women generally corresponds to this threshold. (Paraphrased.)
entries.source_doc: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation
entries.applies_when: adult with documented AFib (paroxysmal, persistent, or permanent)
entries.demo_relevance: Whitaker is on apixaban for AFib — confirms appropriate primary prevention; supports continued anticoagulation.

entries.title: DOACs preferred over warfarin in eligible AFib patients
entries.snippet: For patients with AF (excluding those with moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis or a mechanical heart valve) who are eligible for anticoagulation, DOACs are recommended over warfarin to reduce the risk of stroke or systemic embolism, mortality, and major bleeding (especially intracranial hemorrhage). (Paraphrased.)
entries.source_doc: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation
entries.applies_when: AFib patient without mechanical valve or moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis
entries.demo_relevance: Whitaker on apixaban is on guideline-preferred therapy.

entries.title: Bleeding risk scores inform — do not exclude — anticoagulation
entries.snippet: Bleeding risk scores (e.g., HAS-BLED) should not be used in isolation to determine eligibility for or to discontinue oral anticoagulation but should instead be used to identify and modify reversible bleeding risk factors and to inform shared decision-making. (Paraphrased.)
entries.source_doc: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation
entries.applies_when: patient on or being considered for anticoagulation with bleeding-risk concern
entries.demo_relevance: Whitaker new normocytic anemia + apixaban — bleeding risk does not by itself stop anticoagulation; investigate the source.

entries.title: Anemia in anticoagulated patient: investigate occult GI source
entries.snippet: In asymptomatic postmenopausal women and men with iron deficiency anemia, the AGA recommends bidirectional endoscopy (EGD and colonoscopy) over no endoscopy. Caution and a lower threshold for evaluation are warranted in patients on anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy, in whom identification of a small-bowel or other lesion may change management. (Paraphrased.)
entries.source_doc: AGA Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Gastrointestinal Evaluation of Iron Deficiency Anemia (2020)
entries.applies_when: adult with new IDA or unexplained anemia, especially on anticoagulant/antiplatelet therapy
entries.demo_relevance: Whitaker new normocytic anemia (Hgb 11.1) on apixaban — work up iron studies; if iron-deficient, bidirectional endoscopy.

entries.title: Ferritin <45 ng/mL diagnoses iron deficiency
entries.snippet: In patients with anemia, the AGA recommends using a cutoff of 45 ng/mL over 15 ng/mL when using ferritin to diagnose iron deficiency.
entries.source_doc: AGA Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Gastrointestinal Evaluation of Iron Deficiency Anemia (2020)
entries.applies_when: adult with anemia undergoing iron-status assessment
entries.demo_relevance: Whitaker workup: order ferritin, TSAT, CRP — ferritin <45 supports IDA and triggers GI evaluation.

entries.title: Risk modifiers for borderline cases (eGFR, AF burden, obesity, BP control)
entries.snippet: In patients with AF at intermediate annual stroke risk (<2%/yr), additional factors that may modify risk and inform anticoagulation decisions include higher AF burden (persistent/permanent vs paroxysmal), obesity, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, poorly controlled hypertension, eGFR <45 mL/min, proteinuria >150 mg/24 h, and enlarged left atrial volume (≥73 mL) or diameter (≥4.7 cm). (Paraphrased.)
entries.source_doc: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation
entries.applies_when: AFib patient with borderline (≈1–2%/yr) stroke risk
entries.demo_relevance: Whitaker already anticoagulated — modifiers reinforce decision; relevant in similar patients with CHA2DS2-VASc=1.
